questions.q: What does the `where` operator do in a KQL query like `SigninLogs | where ResultType != "0"`?
options: Renames the ResultType column
Sorts the table by the given column
Keeps only the rows matching the condition and drops the rest
Deletes the matching rows from the underlying table permanently
questions.explain: where filters rows: only rows satisfying the condition continue to the next pipe; nothing is deleted from the underlying data.

questions.q: When you stack two `where` clauses in a row, like `| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d) | where ResultType != "0"`, how do they combine?
options: They act as an OR — a row needs only one condition to survive
KQL rejects a query with more than one where clause
Only the second where clause has any effect
They act as an AND — a row must satisfy both conditions to survive
questions.explain: Each piped where further narrows what came before it, so stacked where clauses behave like an AND between the conditions.

questions.q: What does `project TimeGenerated, UserPrincipalName, IPAddress` do to the result?
options: Keeps only those three columns, in that order, discarding every other column
Adds three new calculated columns to the table
Filters the rows down to only three results
Renames every column in the table to generic names
questions.explain: project selects and orders columns — it reshapes which columns appear in the output, not which rows or how many.

questions.q: What's true about the rows returned by `| take 50` at the end of a query?
options: It returns the 50 rows with the highest ResultType value
It returns every row, but only displays 50 per page
It returns an arbitrary sample of up to 50 matching rows, not necessarily the newest or most severe
It always returns exactly the 50 most recent rows
questions.explain: take (an alias for limit) caps the row count with an arbitrary sample — useful for a quick look, not for a guaranteed top-N list.

questions.q: In `SigninLogs | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d) | where ResultType != "0"`, what does `ago(1d)` return?
options: A timestamp exactly one day before the current time
The exact time the SigninLogs table was created
A Boolean indicating whether a day has passed
A count of how many sign-ins happened in the last day
questions.explain: ago() returns a timestamp that many units before now, so ago(1d) means 24 hours before the query runs.
